Radial centre/periphery pooling

Source: R/hierarchy_poolers.R
radial_pool.Rd

Averages each channel within concentric rings around the centre of the activation map. Use it when distance from the image centre matters and direction does not.

Usage

radial_pool(breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1))

Arguments

breaks

Strictly increasing numeric breakpoints in \([0, 1]\) for normalized radius from the spatial centre. The default c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1) yields three rings.

Value

An imfeatures_pooler that yields length(breaks) - 1 columns per channel.

Details

Radius is measured from the geometric centre of the map and divided by the distance to the corners, so 0 is the centre and 1 is a corner. On a square map the midpoint of each edge lies at about 0.71. Ring k holds positions with breaks[k] <= radius < breaks[k + 1]; the last ring also includes its upper break. Positions outside the range of breaks are left out, so breaks = c(0, 0.5) pools the central region only.

Rings cover unequal numbers of positions. With the default breaks on a 14 x 14 map, the three rings hold 16, 52, and 128 positions. On small maps a ring can hold no positions at all; its columns are then 0 and a warning is raised. The default breaks need a map of about 5 x 5 or larger: on a 4 x 4 map no position lies within 0.25 of the centre, because the centre falls between positions.

Columns are ordered by channel, then ring (centre outwards). Names take the form stage::channel_001::radial_r1.

See also

poolers for the other pooling options.

Examples

# A channel that is active only in the central 2 x 2 positions
a <- array(0, dim = c(1, 8, 8, 1))
a[1, 4:5, 4:5, 1] <- 1
out <- pool_activations(radial_pool(), a)
colnames(out) <- pooler_feature_names(radial_pool(), "b4", 1)
round(out, 3)
#>      b4::channel_001::radial_r1 b4::channel_001::radial_r2
#> [1,]                          1                          0
#>      b4::channel_001::radial_r3
#> [1,]                          0
